bands.name: Plantar calcaneonavicular (spring) ligament

attachments.landmark_b: plantar surface of the navicular

bands.mechanical_role: primary static restraint of the medial longitudinal arch; supports the head of the talus
bands.function_note: Slings the head of the talus from below, with a fibrocartilaginous facet that articulates with it directly. Its attenuation, usually alongside tibialis posterior dysfunction, is a principal mechanism of adult acquired flatfoot -- the talar head drops medially through the failed sling.

bands.name: Bifurcate ligament

attachments.landmark_b: navicular and cuboid, as two limbs

bands.mechanical_role: the key to the midtarsal joint
bands.function_note: Its calcaneal attachment is avulsed in the common 'anterior process of calcaneus' fracture, which is routinely misread as a simple lateral ankle sprain.

bands.name: Lisfranc (interosseous cuneometatarsal) ligament

attachments.landmark_a: lateral surface of the medial cuneiform
attachments.landmark_b: medial base of the second metatarsal

bands.mechanical_role: keys the second metatarsal into the recessed mortise and locks the tarsometatarsal row
bands.function_note: There is no intermetatarsal ligament between the first and second metatarsal bases, so this oblique ligament is the only bond between the medial and middle columns. Its disruption is the Lisfranc injury; a widened first-second interspace on a weight-bearing film is the sign, and missed injuries lead to midfoot collapse and arthritis.

name_ta: Ligamenta plantaria et collateralia articulationis metatarsophalangealis I
name_common: 1st MTP joint plantar plate and collateral ligaments

attachments.landmark_b: proximal phalanx of the hallux, plantar and lateral/medial bases

bands.name: Plantar plate (of the 1st MTP joint)

attachments.landmark_a: 1st metatarsal neck, plantar aspect (thin, weak proximal attachment)
attachments.landmark_b: plantar base of the proximal phalanx of the hallux (strong distal attachment)

bands.mechanical_role: primary static restraint against hyperextension (dorsiflexion) of the 1st MTP joint; houses and anchors the medial and lateral sesamoid bones
bands.function_note: A dense fibrocartilaginous thickening of the plantar joint capsule, continuous with the flexor hallucis brevis tendon sheath and anchoring the sesamoid bones via the sesamoid-phalangeal ligaments. It is far weaker at its proximal (metatarsal) attachment than at its distal (phalangeal) attachment, so acute hyperextension injury -- 'turf toe' -- characteristically tears or avulses the plate near its metatarsal-neck origin rather than at the phalangeal end.
bands.source: Pfahl K, Weber C, Walther M (2023) 'Posttraumatic Pathologies of the First Metatarsophalangeal Joint.' Foot Ankle Clin 30(1):157-171, doi:10.1016/j.fcl.2023.09.005 (https://doi.org/10.1016/j.fcl.2023.09.005) -- retrieved via PubMed

bands.name: Medial collateral ligament (of the 1st MTP joint)

attachments.landmark_b: proximal phalanx of the hallux, medial base

bands.mechanical_role: resists valgus (abduction) angulation of the hallux at the MTP joint
bands.function_note: Comprises a proper component (metatarsal to phalanx) and a deeper accessory component (metatarsal to sesamoid/plantar plate). Chronic attenuation of this medial-sided soft-tissue restraint contributes to the progressive lateral deviation of the hallux seen in hallux valgus.
bands.source: Pfahl K, Weber C, Walther M (2023) 'Posttraumatic Pathologies of the First Metatarsophalangeal Joint.' Foot Ankle Clin 30(1):157-171, doi:10.1016/j.fcl.2023.09.005 (https://doi.org/10.1016/j.fcl.2023.09.005) -- retrieved via PubMed

bands.name: Lateral collateral ligament (of the 1st MTP joint)

attachments.landmark_b: proximal phalanx of the hallux, lateral base

bands.mechanical_role: resists varus (adduction) angulation of the hallux; together with the medial collateral ligament provides the joint's primary coronal-plane stability
bands.function_note: Also has proper and accessory (sesamoidal) components mirroring the medial collateral ligament; injured, together with the plantar plate, in the valgus-stress pattern of some turf toe injuries.
bands.source: Pfahl K, Weber C, Walther M (2023) 'Posttraumatic Pathologies of the First Metatarsophalangeal Joint.' Foot Ankle Clin 30(1):157-171, doi:10.1016/j.fcl.2023.09.005 (https://doi.org/10.1016/j.fcl.2023.09.005) -- retrieved via PubMed

function: The capsuloligamentous complex of the great toe's MTP joint -- the plantar plate and paired collateral ligaments -- together provide the joint's primary static stability, resisting hyperextension and coronal-plane (valgus/varus) angulation under the high loads of terminal stance and push-off. Acute hyperextension injury of this complex is the athletic injury 'turf toe'; its chronic attenuation is a contributing mechanism in hallux valgus deformity.
source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998); Pfahl K, Weber C, Walther M (2023) 'Posttraumatic Pathologies of the First Metatarsophalangeal Joint.' Foot Ankle Clin 30(1):157-171, doi:10.1016/j.fcl.2023.09.005 -- retrieved via PubMed
